newsitem.title: FRANCE: Peugeot takes stake in Argentina's Sevel.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot takes stake in Argentina's Sevel.

text.p: French carmaker Automobiles Peugeot has agreed to take a minority stake in Sevel Argentina as part of a drive to boost its presence in Latin America and other fast-growing markets, Peugeot officials said.

Peugeot, a division of PSA Peugeot Citroen, will initially take 15 percent of Sevel, controlled by Argentina's Macri group, for $35 million as part of a capital increase, Peugeot deputy managing director Yves Barbe told a news conference.
It plans to raise that stake to 23 percent next year for about the same amount. "We haven't ruled out future changes in the capital structure or production plans," Barbe said.

He said the PSA group also expects to make an announcement soon on plans to start production in Brazil, joining Fiat, Ford, Volkswagen, Renault and others gearing up to meet an expected surge in demand for cars.
The PSA group has said it was considering producing around 70,000 cars a year in Brazil for the Mercosur free trade zone which groups Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay and Argentina.

It is targeting Latin America, eastern Europe and southeast Asia in an effort to roughly double the share of its sales outside western Europe to 25 percent from 13 percent in 1996. It wants to lessen its dependence on western Europe's mature car market, which is expected to grow just two percent this year.

Automobiles Peugeot last year sold 47,000 cars in Argentina, or 12.9 percent of the market which grew nearly 15 percent. It is aiming for a 15 percent share, and Automobiles Citroen, which had 1.2 percent, wants three to five percent, officials said.
Sevel turned out 65,000 Peugeot vehicles under licence last year, including the 504 and 504 pickup, the 405 sedan and smaller 306 car, but that represents less than half of its production capacity.
It will start making the Peugeot Partner and Citroen Berlingo light commercial vehicles next year at the Palomar plant, the only Latin American production site for those models.
Sevel Argentina was formed in 1980 with the merger of Fiat Automobiles and Safrar Peugeot SA, and the Macri group acquired control two years later.
Last year, it stopped producing vehicles under licence for Fiat, which established its own production site in Argentina.
Sevel is also the exclusive importer of Citroen vehicles.
